_README: Licence manifest for every NON-PIP artifact Nightjar's phase2-mcp fetches, vendors,
or trains on: model weights, ONNX graphs, voice packs, and training datasets.
Why this file exists: test_no_copyleft_venv.py (#146) sweeps installed Python
DISTRIBUTIONS. It is blind to everything that arrives as a download at runtime or
as a checked-in binary — which is exactly where NJ-58 lived. openWakeWord's CODE is
Apache-2.0 and sailed through that guard while its bundled MODEL WEIGHTS were
CC-BY-NC-SA. A package-level guard cannot catch a weights-level licence.
tests/test_model_licenses.py enforces this file. Adding an artifact without an
entry here FAILS the build; so does a checksum drift, or a non-commercial /
Rule 5 applies verbatim: `license` must come from a licence FILE or a licence
statement read at `license_read_from` — never a repo badge, never a `license:`
field taken on trust, never an inference from a sibling artifact.

artifacts.role: TTS model weights (Kokoro-82M) — spoken replies, and since PR 5 also the wake-word training-positive generator
artifacts.license_read_from: https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M — model card frontmatter `license: apache-2.0` plus the repo LICENSE file
notes: The weights are Kokoro-82M's; the kokoro-onnx GitHub release is only a redistribution
of them in ONNX form (that package itself is MIT and is no longer a dependency — only
its 114-entry phoneme table is vendored, as kokoro_vocab.json).
PR 5 widened this artifact's role: it now also generates wake-word TRAINING POSITIVES.
That is a different exercise of the same Apache-2.0 grant (no field-of-use restriction,
no output clause), and it is the specific reason Nightjar can drop Piper — see the
`REJECTED-piper-*` entries below.

artifacts.role: Kokoro voice style-vector packs (54 voices, 28 of them English)
artifacts.license_read_from: https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M — same repo and licence as the weights; the voice packs ship in that repo under voices/
notes: 54 .pt voice packs. English subset used for training positives: af_* (11), am_* (9),
bf_* (4), bm_* (4) = 28. The remainder are es/fr/hi/it/ja/pt/zh.

artifacts.role: Wake-word front end: 16 kHz PCM -> 32-bin log-mel, 10 ms hop
artifacts.copyright: torchlibrosa (© Qiuqiang Kong), exported to ONNX
artifacts.license_read_from: hey-buddy GitHub README § License ("source code and pretrained models are released under the Apache License 2.0"); upstream lineage credited in that README to torchlibrosa
notes: VERIFIED BY RUNNING, not by reading (PR 5): this file is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the
melspectrogram.onnx shipped inside the openwakeword wheel — same sha256. That matters
because openWakeWord's README blanket-claims 'All of the included pre-trained models
are licensed under CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0'. A file that a second project independently
publishes under Apache-2.0/CC-BY-4.0, bit for bit, is evidence that the blanket
sentence over-reaches rather than that this artifact is non-commercial.
See the hey-buddy licence conflict noted on speech-embedding.onnx: the GitHub README
says Apache-2.0, the HF repo card says cc-by-4.0. We comply with the stricter (CC-BY).

artifacts.role: Wake-word backbone: 76x32 mel window -> 96-d embedding (frozen feature extractor)
artifacts.copyright: © Google LLC (speech_embedding); ONNX conversion by benjamin-paine
artifacts.license_read_from: PRIMARY SOURCE: https://www.kaggle.com/models/google/speech-embedding — model card 'About Variation' states LICENSE: Apache 2.0, SOURCE: TensorFlow, Fine-tunable: Yes (maintainer-verified in a browser, 2026-08-03, screenshot archived). Redistribution licence per hey-buddy GitHub README § License.
notes: This closes NJ-58's backbone question, which upstream openWakeWord never answered
(issues #313 and #338, both 0 comments, both still open).
Two independent confirmations, one read and one RUN:
(a) READ: the Kaggle model card for google/speech-embedding states Apache-2.0.
(b) RUN (PR 5): loading this file and openwakeword's embedding_model.onnx side by
side shows 37 shared weight initializers, ALL numerically identical, and both
files carry producer_name 'tf2onnx' (1.12.1 here, 1.9.3 there). They are two
conversions of the SAME TensorFlow network. The weights are Google's.
The two graphs are NOT interchangeable despite the shared weights: openWakeWord's
inserts an extra Pad before the first Reshape and a Relu+BatchNormalization after the
first Conv, which shifts activations (per-row cosine ~0.977 on the same input). A wake
model must be scored with the same backbone it was trained against, so Nightjar ships
THIS one. That is an empirical constraint, not a preference.
LICENCE CONFLICT, unresolved upstream: hey-buddy's GitHub README says its pretrained
models are Apache-2.0; the HuggingFace repo that actually serves this file (hard-coded
as pretrained_model_url in embeddings.py) declares `license: cc-by-4.0`. Both permit
commercial use. We comply with the stricter reading and attribute.

artifacts.role: INTERIM stand-in wake model — the phrase is 'hey buddy', not 'hey june'
artifacts.commercial_ok_reason: Upstream labels it Apache-2.0/CC-BY-4.0, but its POSITIVES were generated with Piper en_US-libritts_r-medium, whose lineage traces to Lessac Blizzard 2013 — a licence that forbids exactly this use (NJ-59). Shippable in a free build; must NOT ship in a paid build.
artifacts.license_read_from: hey-buddy GitHub README § License; HF repo card frontmatter `license: cc-by-4.0`
notes: Replaces the CC-BY-NC-SA `hey_jarvis_v0.1.onnx` that Nightjar fell back to before PR 5.
Strictly better on every axis: the NON-COMMERCIAL artifact leaves the tree entirely
(NJ-58 resolved), and the residual problem is narrower and named (NJ-59).
It is loaded with is_custom=False so the pre-existing loud startup warning still fires,
and it exists mainly so the runtime path is EXERCISABLE end-to-end before our own model
is trained — which is what let PR 5 verify the new onnxruntime shim by running it
against a real model instead of reasoning about the port (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
Retire this entry the moment hey_june.onnx lands.

artifacts.role: Training negatives + validation set: ~23.3M x 17 x 96 float16 embeddings, ~6,500 h
artifacts.license_read_from: HF dataset card frontmatter `license: cc-by-4.0` + its per-source licence table
notes: 18 constituent corpora, every one permissive per the card's own table: parler-tts/mls_eng
(CC-BY-4.0), mozilla-foundation/common_voice_17_0 en/de/fr/es/eo/sw/zh-CN/ar/hi (CC0-1.0),
homebrewltd/instruction-speech-encodec-v1 (MIT), MushanW/GLOBE (CC0-1.0),
facebook/voxpopuli en (CC0-1.0), benjamin-paine/freesound-laion-640k (CC0/CC-BY),
benjamin-paine/dinner-party-corpus (CDLA-Permissive-1.0), google/fleurs en_us (CC-BY-4.0).
Validation adds gpt-omni/VoiceAssistant-400K (Apache-2.0).
NO PIPER TAINT HERE — this set is negatives (real recorded speech) and carries none of
the synthetic positives. NJ-59 lives entirely in the positive/adversarial stage, which
Nightjar replaces with Kokoro.
NOT YET MIRRORED. The brief is to self-host rather than hot-link, and 72 GB needs object
storage that does not exist yet. mirror_datasets.py emits the shard list + checksums;
running it against a real bucket is a maintainer action in the training PR.
RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: the per-source licences above are upstream's own
table. Each has been sanity-checked against its HF card, but a full primary read of all
18 corpora's licence files is outstanding and belongs with the mirroring work.

artifacts.role: was: hey-buddy's default reverb augmentation — REJECTED, substituted by openslr-26-simulated-rirs
artifacts.license_read_from: exhaustive primary-source search, training PR 2026-08-03 — see notes
notes: NJ-60(b), resolved by SUBSTITUTION rather than clearance. Searched, in order:
(a) mcdermottlab.mit.edu/Reverb/IR_Survey.html — the distribution page: NO licence,
terms, or conditions language anywhere in the page source (grepped, not skimmed);
(b) the Audio.zip download itself (11.6 MB, fetched): 271 WAVs + .DS_Store —
no README, no LICENSE, nothing;
(c) github.com/jtraer/IR_Analysis_Synthesis (the paper's code): license: null.
The HF repacker's 'CC-BY 4.0' frontmatter is therefore an UNSUPPORTED assertion —
no grant exists at any primary source, which defaults to all-rights-reserved.
This is exactly the laundering pattern rule 5 exists to catch: a downstream label
with no upstream grant behind it.
Training uses openslr-26-simulated-rirs instead (next entry). If the McDermott lab
ever publishes actual terms, this entry can be revisited — until then it stays
rejected, and mirror_datasets.py refuses to mirror it (verified by running: the
plan step blocks it).

artifacts.role: Training augmentation: room impulse responses (reverb) — the NJ-60 substitute
artifacts.license_read_from: openslr.org/26 resource page ('License: Apache 2.0'); provenance READMEs read from inside the SLR28 zip via ranged fetch (training PR, 2026-08-03)
notes: 60,000 simulated room impulse responses (600 rooms x 100 speaker/receiver positions,
image method), generated BY THE SLR28/26 AUTHORS THEMSELVES — first-party synthetic
data with no upstream corpus lineage, which is what makes the Apache-2.0 label
coherent where the MIT set's CC-BY claim was not. The in-zip simulated_rirs/README
(read without downloading the 1.3 GB archive, via HTTP range requests into the zip's
central directory) documents the generation pipeline and parameters.
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from use: SLR28's real_rirs_isotropic_noises subset — it is
composed of RWCP + REVERB-2014 + AIR, each with its OWN terms we have not read;
using it would reintroduce the exact unverified-lineage problem the substitution
solves. Train only with RIRS_NOISES/simulated_rirs (SLR26 standalone = same data).
Caveat, stated: the Apache-2.0 grant is the OpenSLR resource-page label; the zip
itself carries no top-level LICENSE file for this subset. Page label + first-party
provenance is the strongest evidence available and is judged sufficient for
training-side use; recorded here rather than glossed.
Upstream describes the constituent clips as CC0 / CC-BY / CC-Sampling+. The 'commercial'
in the repo name is the maintainer's own pre-filter of the LAION Freesound set.
Constituents per upstream: CC0, CC-BY, CC-Sampling+, FMA Sound Recording Common Law,
Free Art License, Public Domain. Free Art License is copyleft-ish for the WORK, but
these are background-noise mixes in a training signal, not redistributed recordings.
Flagged here so a future strict-relicense review sees it.

artifacts.role: was: hey-buddy's default TTS for training positives + adversarials
notes: NJ-59. The chain, each link read as primary source:
libritts_r/medium MODEL_CARD: 'Fine-tuned from English lessac medium on train-clean-360.'
lessac/medium MODEL_CARD: trained from scratch on Lessac Blizzard 2013.
Blizzard 2013 licence: 'Research Purposes' ... 'excludes ... developing, adapting,
amending or otherwise using the Materials for any commercial purpose, including the
development, marketing, commercialisation, sale or licencing of voice synthesis or
speech recognition products or services'.
That last clause names Nightjar's exact use case. Note LibriTTS-R itself is CC-BY-4.0 —
the encumbrance is the lessac CHECKPOINT the voice was fine-tuned FROM, which is why
reading only the dataset licence would have missed it.
Replaced by Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0). Recorded fallback if Kokoro's 28 English voices
prove insufficient: a from-scratch LibriTTS voice (CC-BY-4.0, 2,456 speakers) — NOT
anything fine-tuned from lessac.
The old wakeword_training/README.md instructed a future maintainer to use exactly this.
Kept as an explicit rejection so nobody follows that instruction from an old checkout,
and so the two independent paths into the same taint (openWakeWord's recommendation AND
hey-buddy's built-in default) are both recorded.
